open_points.subject: K-09 store-refusal scope
open_points.text: the kernel stops because the store refused its record
open_points.question: What exactly stops when the trace record is refused: the node, its run, admission of all new work, or the kernel process?
options: Stop only this node and run
Stop this run but continue other runs
Stop the whole kernel process
open_points.default_guess: Stop the affected run and reject new work until the store is healthy.

witness.initial: Two runs are active when one node's trace record is refused.
events: The store refuses run A's trace record.
Run B has a ready node.
outcomes: Run B continues because only run A stopped.
Run B also stops because the kernel process stopped.
witness.observer: The owner waiting for run B

open_points.subject: K-09 trace commit boundary
open_points.text: An execution during which the kernel stops because the store refused its record leaves none
open_points.question: Must the trace record commit before the node's output can be exposed to downstream nodes or any caller?
options: Commit the trace before publishing output
Publish output before attempting the trace write
Allow publication and retract it if the trace write fails
open_points.default_guess: Commit the trace before publishing any output.

witness.initial: A function can obtain chance by an undetected route and may return different values on two executions.
events: The first execution returns A.
A downstream node is ready to consume the result.
The store refuses the first execution's trace record.
Recovery executes the function again and it returns B.
outcomes: The downstream node sees only B because output was held until the trace committed.
The downstream node has already seen A while the recovered trace records B.
witness.observer: The downstream node and the owner reading traces

open_points.subject: K-09 recovery of effectful operation nodes
open_points.text: recovery executes it again / The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key and never repeats an effect without a fresh approval. / When the kernel cannot tell whether an effect happened, the run rests `pending` with reason `outcome_unknown` and only the owner's resolution moves it
open_points.question: When an effectful operation completed but its trace record was refused, does recovery execute it automatically, or must the run become `outcome_unknown` and wait for the owner's resolution and any required fresh approval?
options: Always execute it again during recovery
Wait for owner resolution and fresh approval before another invocation
Replay automatically only when the service can prove the original idempotency key was applied
open_points.default_guess: Rest `pending` as `outcome_unknown`; require owner resolution and a fresh approval before any resend.

witness.initial: A destructive node has one approval and targets an existing object.
events: The service deletes the object.
The store refuses the execution's trace record.
The kernel recovers without durable evidence of the service result.
outcomes: K-09 causes recovery to invoke the destructive operation again.
K-08 leaves the run pending for owner resolution and forbids another invocation without fresh approval.
witness.observer: The owner and the target service

open_points.subject: K-09 recovered operation identity
open_points.question: For a recovered operation node, must the second invocation use the same target, exact input, pinned binding and idempotency key as the unrecorded invocation, or is it a new invocation with a new key?
options: Replay the exact request with the same idempotency key
Use the same request with a new idempotency key
Reconstruct the request from current records and bindings
open_points.default_guess: Replay the pinned request with the same idempotency key, after satisfying K-08 approval and resolution rules.

witness.initial: An operation creates a charge using idempotency key K, and its trace write is refused.
events: The service accepts the charge under K.
Recovery invokes the node again.
outcomes: Recovery reuses K and the service deduplicates the request.
Recovery creates a new key and the service creates a second charge.
witness.observer: The owner and the external service

open_points.subject: K-09 recovery detection
open_points.text: leaves none, and recovery executes it again
open_points.question: What durable fact identifies that an execution with no trace must be executed again, including its run, node or map item, pinned versions and input?
options: A durable pre-execution attempt marker outside the trace
A run cursor or ready-node state from which recovery derives the work
Scan the graph and infer every node lacking a trace
No durable marker; an operator identifies the work
open_points.default_guess: Persist a pre-execution attempt marker and its exact replay input before starting the node.

witness.initial: A run has two ready mapped executions and neither yet has a trace.
events: One mapped execution starts.
Its trace record is refused and the kernel stops.
The kernel starts recovery.
outcomes: A durable marker identifies and repeats only the started item.
Absence of traces makes recovery repeat both items or neither item.
witness.observer: The owner and any invoked service

open_points.subject: K-09 recovery initiation
open_points.question: Who starts recovery, by what product action, and when: automatically on process restart, through `resume`, or through an operator-only procedure?
options: Automatic recovery at kernel startup
Owner or agent invokes `resume`
An operator repairs the store and explicitly starts recovery
open_points.default_guess: Automatically identify the interrupted run at startup, but require `resume` for non-effectful work and K-08 resolution for uncertain effects.

open_points.subject: K-09 run state after trace refusal
open_points.text: the kernel stops because the store refused its record
open_points.question: What durable run and node status represents this condition before recovery, given that the listed waiting states cover approval, unreachable services and unknown outcomes but not a refused trace write?
options: `pending` with a new store-related reason
`failed`
A distinct recovery-required state
Retain `running` and recover interrupted work from it

witness.initial: A node finishes and its trace record is refused.
events: The kernel stops.
The owner later inspects the run before recovery completes.
outcomes: The run is reported `pending` and can be deliberately resumed.
The run remains `running`, is reported `failed`, or cannot be classified.
witness.observer: The owner inspecting the run through MCP

open_points.subject: K-09 refusal classification
open_points.question: Which store outcomes count as refusal requiring recovery: transient unavailability, transaction conflict, capacity exhaustion, validation failure, an oversized record, or every unsuccessful commit?
options: Every unsuccessful trace transaction
Only transient storage failures
Only failures for which atomic non-commit is proven
Different handling by refusal class
open_points.default_guess: Treat every proven atomic non-commit as an interrupted attempt, while permanent validation or size failures terminate the run with a distinct failure.

open_points.subject: K-09 repeated recovery failure
open_points.question: What happens if the store continues refusing the recovered execution's trace record, or the refusal is permanent?
options: Retry without limit
Retry a bounded number of times and fail the run
Remain pending until an owner or agent resumes
Refuse kernel startup until an operator repairs the store
open_points.default_guess: Keep the run pending without automatic retry loops and permit another attempt only after an explicit resume or operator-confirmed repair.

witness.initial: The trace record permanently violates a store constraint.
events: The first trace write is refused.
Recovery executes the node again.
The identical trace write is refused again.
outcomes: The kernel repeatedly executes and stops forever.
The run reaches a stable pending or failed state with an observable reason.
witness.observer: The owner and the kernel operator

open_points.subject: K-09 unrecorded value and file artifacts
open_points.question: Does `leaves none` mean only that no trace exists, or must recovery also discard bounded values, spool files and other kernel artifacts produced by the unrecorded execution before executing it again?
options: Only the trace is absent; artifacts remain
All kernel artifacts of the attempt are atomically absent or removed
Artifacts are retained and adopted by the recovered execution
open_points.default_guess: Remove or quarantine every kernel artifact from the unrecorded attempt before rerunning it.

witness.initial: A function writes a file into the run spool and then its trace record is refused.
events: The first spool file remains after the kernel stops.
Recovery executes the function and produces another file.
outcomes: Recovery deletes the first file and only the recovered output can travel onward.
Both files remain, or the first is mistakenly selected as the recovered output.
witness.observer: The next node, the owner, and the storage operator

open_points.subject: K-09 recoverable input retention
open_points.question: What guarantees that the exact input needed for re-execution, especially a file in the run spool, survives whatever `the kernel stops` means?
options: The run spool and edge values are durable across process restarts
Recovery re-executes upstream nodes to reconstruct missing inputs
Recovery is guaranteed only while the original inputs remain available
Missing input makes the run fail or await owner action
open_points.default_guess: Make all inputs of a started node, including spool files, durable until its trace commits or its run ends.

witness.initial: An operation node's input is a file produced earlier in the same run.
events: The operation executes.
Its trace record is refused and the kernel process stops.
The process restarts without an in-memory spool.
outcomes: A durable spool permits exact re-execution.
The input is gone, so the promised recovery cannot execute the node again.
witness.observer: The owner attempting to recover the run

open_points.subject: K-09 execution-attempt identity
open_points.text: Every node execution writes one immutable trace record / recovery executes it again
open_points.question: Is the recovered execution the same logical execution, a new attempt of the same node execution, or a second node execution, and how are attempts identified in traces and resource accounting?
options: One logical execution with numbered attempts
The unrecorded attempt does not count and recovery is the sole execution
Recovery is a distinct execution linked to an interrupted predecessor
open_points.default_guess: Model one logical node execution with durable, numbered attempts and record the recovered attempt plus an interruption marker.

open_points.subject: K-09 store-refusal observability
open_points.text: the store refused its record leaves none
open_points.question: What observable output tells the owner or operator that a trace write was refused, when the failed attempt deliberately leaves no trace?
options: A durable run-level recovery reason stored separately
An out-of-store operational log or alert
A refusal returned synchronously to the caller
No direct notice; only recovery behavior reveals it
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct failure to any active caller and expose a durable run-level recovery reason that is not the missing trace.

witness.initial: The owner invokes `run` while the store can update no trace records.
events: The node executes.
The store refuses its trace record.
The kernel stops before recovery.
outcomes: The owner receives a distinct store-refusal result or alert.
The call disconnects or appears unfinished with no record explaining why.
witness.observer: The owner and the kernel operator
